title: Extensions and preset contracts
summary: Build extension ordering, guarded Material addon transformations and bounded preset setup, provider and substitution contracts.

facts.claim: For each built field, Formly runs extension prePopulate hooks, then onPopulate hooks, recursively builds children, then runs postPopulate hooks.
conditions: The Formly 6.3.12 builder processes a field.
limits: These build extension hooks are distinct from field/component lifecycle hooks such as onInit.
This ordering does not establish a once-only execution guarantee for arbitrary extensions.
facts.context: Extension phase order and child traversal versus onInit lifecycle.
facts.source_quote: The builder runs extension `prePopulate`, `onPopulate`, child building, then `postPopulate`. Extension hooks differ from component/field lifecycle hooks such as `onInit`. Extensions are sorted by ascending priority; the core registrations use negative priorities, while an unspecified custom priority defaults to 1. Verify dependencies rather than assuming registration order determines every stage. [K06](sources.md#k06), [K03](sources.md#k03), [K35](sources.md#k35)

facts.claim: Formly orders extensions by ascending numeric priority; an unspecified priority defaults to 1, while the built-in core registrations have negative priorities.
conditions: Extension configurations are registered with Formly 6.3.12.
limits: Do not assume registration order alone determines execution when priorities differ.
A lower priority runs earlier within each extension phase; dependencies still need verification.
facts.context: Ordering custom extensions relative to core and one another; higher priorities run later.
facts.source_quote: The builder runs extension `prePopulate`, `onPopulate`, child building, then `postPopulate`. Extension hooks differ from component/field lifecycle hooks such as `onInit`. facts.claim: The pinned Material addons example conditionally appends its addons wrapper and checks for an existing wrapper before appending.
conditions: The example has addon props and does not already contain the addons wrapper.
limits: The guard illustrates an idempotent transformation; it does not prove arbitrary extensions safe to rerun.
This is an example pattern, not evidence that addons is a universally registered core wrapper or a complete custom component recipe.
facts.context: Avoid duplicate wrapper insertion on repeated builds; Material prefix and suffix extension example.
facts.source_quote: The Material addons example conditionally appends a wrapper and checks whether it is already present. That guard is a useful model for idempotent transformations when a field is rebuilt. It is an example, not proof that an arbitrary extension is safe to rerun. [E06](examples.md#e06)

facts.claim: Formly presets use FormlyPresetModule from @ngx-formly/core/preset, named presets configuration, and a field type reference prefixed with #.
conditions: The pinned Formly 6.3.12 preset feature is configured.
limits: A #name reference is preset syntax, not proof that the same unprefixed name is a registered rendering type.
The referenced preset and any rendering type it supplies still need configuration.
facts.context: Import FormlyPresetModule, provide presets entries, select reusable configuration with type: #name.
facts.source_quote: The v6 guide uses `FormlyPresetModule` from `@ngx-formly/core/preset`, configuration `presets`, and a `#name` reference. The implementation substitutes configuration during prePopulate at priority -300, before core initialization. It supports a configuration provider's `getConfiguration()`. Complex/recursive composition remains unqualified. Read [API contracts](api-contracts.md) for merge semantics before relying on empty/null overrides. [K23](sources.md#k23), [K44](sources.md#k44)

facts.claim: A Formly preset configuration can be supplied by a provider with a getConfiguration() method.
conditions: The configured preset uses the provider contract in Formly 6.3.12.
limits: This does not establish asynchronous provider handling or recursive preset composition.
A plain configuration object is also supported; a provider is not required for every preset.
facts.context: Reusable named configuration from a FormlyFieldConfigPresetProvider getConfiguration method.
facts.source_quote: The v6 guide uses `FormlyPresetModule` from `@ngx-formly/core/preset`, configuration `presets`, and a `#name` reference. facts.claim: The Formly preset substitution extension replaces #name configuration during prePopulate with priority -300, before core initialization.
conditions: A matching configured preset is referenced by the field in Formly 6.3.12.
limits: Complex or recursive preset composition remains unqualified.
Do not infer arbitrary empty/null override or recursive merge semantics from substitution timing.
facts.context: Preset substitution before core extension initialization rather than during onInit or postPopulate.
